headline: Regional Official Proposes Integrating Neighbouring Territory Using A Shared WhatsApp Group
body:
A senior regional administrator has suggested that the most effective way to unify a disputed neighbouring territory would be to create a 'Greater Regional Coordination' WhatsApp group, provided the administrators agree to regular 'Good Morning' stickers and disable the 'only admins can post' setting.

The proposal, outlined during a cabinet meeting on Tuesday, suggests that once the group is formed, the neighbouring administration would naturally be compelled to join the statehood fold by the sheer volume of high-resolution flower images and inspirational quotes shared by the local department of rural development.

'It is really about the vibe,' said a spokesperson for the local bureaucracy, requesting anonymity. 'If we start by adding their regional representatives to a group titled "Unified Development & Snacks," the friction of border management will immediately be replaced by the inevitable social pressure to participate in a Secret Santa exchange by December.'

Critics of the plan have pointed out that the neighbouring administration might simply leave the group or mute notifications. However, the spokesperson insisted that the 'typing...' bubble appearing on their screens for hours at a time would create enough psychological intimacy to render physical borders irrelevant by the next fiscal quarter.
caption: Forget policy—it is time for group admin powers to handle regional integration. Will a shared 'Good Morning' sticker finally solve it all? #Politics #Integration #TechSolutions (satire)

Its specific invented details—the 'Good Morning' stickers, the 'Secret Santa' pressure, and the psychological impact of the 'typing...' bubble—create a much more vivid and grounded satirical premise than the broader tech or food-based tropes in the other entries.
